title: Electric Terrain

sections.heading: Description
lines: Electric Terrain is one of the Field Effects present in Rejuvenation. It is categorized as an Elemental field.

sections.heading: Transitions From Other Fields
lines: No other Field Effect can be in place for the field to be created. If another Field Effect is present when the Electric Terrain is generated, the original Field remains active, and the Electric Terrain has fewer effects than normal. These will be highlighted by an underline.

Electric Terrain cannot be overlayed over Frozen Dimensional Field or Underwater Field. If the field changes to Frozen Dimensional Field, the overlay will last until it is destroyed by a move. If the field changes to Underwater Field, the overlay will be destroyed. Electric Terrain overlay disappears if a different overlay is set while it's still active.
Short-Circuit Field's damage rolls are always maximal when overlayed with Electric Terrain.
This field is generated by:
The abilities Electric Surge and Hadron Engine on switch-in and the move Electric Terrain, for 5 turns normally and 8 turns if the Pokémon holds an Amplifield Rock.
Raikou's Crest for 5 turns.
The moves Plasma Fists and Ion Deluge if the user does not hold a working Everstone for 3 turns normally and 6 turns if the user holds an Amplifield Rock.
The Z-Move Stoked Sparksurfer for 3 turns.

sections.heading: General Effects
lines: Electric-type moves from grounded Pokémon increase in base power by 1.5x. (1.3x when overlayed)
“The Electric Terrain strengthened the attack!”
Grounded Pokémon cannot fall asleep.
“[Pokémon] is protected by the Electric Terrain!”

sections.heading: Abilities Affected
lines: Activated Abilities:
Hadron Engine
“[Pokémon] used the Electric Terrain to energize its futuristic engine!”
Quark Drive
“The Electric Terrain activated [Pokémon]'s Quark Drive, heightening its [Stat]!”
Minus
Plus
Surge Surfer
Quick Feet
Buffed Abilities:
Steadfast multiplies the user's Speed by 1.5x.
Volt Absorb heals 1/16 max HP at the end of each turn.
“[Pokémon] absorbed stray electricity!”
Battery boosts allies' Special Attack by 1.5x instead of 1.3x.
Electromorphosis and Lightning Rod boost the user's Special Attack by 1 stage on switch in.
Galvanize increases base power by 1.5x for affected moves instead of 1.2x.
Motor Drive raises the user's Speed by 1 stage at the end of each turn.
Slow Start timer counts down twice as fast.
This translates to its user getting it together in 3 turns.
Static has a doubled chance to activate (60%).
Teravolt lets the user's Electric-type moves deal neutral damage to Ground-types.
Transistor boosts the damage of the user's Electric-type moves by 1.6x instead of 1.3x.
Nerfed Abilities:
Comatose is disabled.
Other Ability changes:
Gulp Missile always picks up Pikachu.

sections.heading: Moves Affected
lines: Damage modifiers: Moves which receive an attack buff:
Magnet Bomb → 2x boost.
“The attack powered-up!”
Explosion, Hurricane, Muddy Water, Self-Destruct, Smack Down, Surf, Thousand Arrows, Hydro Vortex → 1.5x boost, Electric sub-typing.
“The attack became hyper-charged!”
“The explosion became hyper-charged!”
Wildbolt Storm → 1.5x boost.
“The attack became hyper-charged!”
Psyblade → 1.5x boost.
Inherent effect of the move.
Rising Voltage → 2x Boost against grounded targets.
Inherent effect of the move.
Moves which receive an attack nerf:
Focus Punch → Fails upon use.
“[Pokémon] lost its focus and couldn't move!”
Other effects: Buffed moves:
Magnet Rise lasts for 8 turns.
Pokémon under the effects of Magnet Rise still benefit from the Terrain's buff to Electric-type moves.
Charge boosts the user's Special Defense by 2 stages.
Eerie Impulse lowers the target's Special Attack by 3 stages.
Electro Shot requires no charge turn.
Electrify additionally turns the target into the Electric type.
As of V14.0.22, this effect is not listed in the in-game Field Notes.
Electroweb lowers all targets' Speed by 2 stages.
Magnetic Flux boosts all allies' Defense and Special Defense by 2 stages if they have the Plus or Minus ability, or 1 stage otherwise.
Parabolic Charge heals 75% of damage dealt.
Thunder Cage deals 1/6th max HP damage at the end of each turn instead of 1/8th.
Wild Charge no longer has recoil.
Other move changes:
Spikes deals Electric-type scaling damage and can hit airborne Pokémon.
This effect applies even if Spikes were set up before the creation of the Electric Terrain.
“[Pokémon] was hurt by the electrified spikes!”

sections.heading: Field-dependent moves & abilities
lines: Mimicry changes the user's type to Electric.
Camouflage changes the user's type to Electric.
Nature Power becomes Thunderbolt.
Secret Power may inflict Paralysis.
Shelter halves damage from Electric-type moves.
Terrain Pulse becomes Electric-type.

sections.heading: Transitions to Other Fields
lines: Any move in this section inherently gains a 1.3x damage boost on top of any other previously listed modifiers.
The Z-Move Tectonic Rage will terminate this field.
The move Mud Sport will disable the field while the move effect lasts.
“The hyper-charged terrain shorted out!”

sections.heading: Items
lines: Elemental Seed boosts the user's Speed by 1 stage and applies Charge to the user.
Cell Battery is consumed and boosts the holder's Attack by 1 stage on switch in.

sections.heading: Notes
lines: Prior to V14, some abilities possessed different effects in this terrain (these did not apply to overlayed terrains):
Transistor instead reduced the base power of Ground-type moves against the user by 0.5x instead of further boosting Electric-type moves.
Teravolt increased the damage of electric moves by 1.5x on top of its current effect.
Electric Terrain is one of the four Field Effects present in the mainline Pokémon series, although its canonical counterpart applies less effects.
